summary: Defines an experimental portion of the MIB for managing OSI connectionless networks (ISO 8473 and ISO 9542). It is an Experimental document.

eli5.summary: It is a checklist for monitoring a kind of network that follows another standards family.

subtitle: SNMP management objects for monitoring OSI connectionless network (CLNP) and ES-IS implementations.

tldr.problem: Network managers using TCP/IP management tools had no standard set of variables for monitoring systems that run the OSI Connectionless-mode Network Protocol (ISO 8473) and the ES-IS protocol (ISO 9542).
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines an experimental MIB module, CLNS-MIB, with four groups (clnp, error, echo, es-is), mostly read-only counters plus tables for addresses, routes and address translation.
tldr.outcome: It is an Experimental document that obsoletes RFC 1162, restating the same semantics in the concise MIB format and adding a few objects.

today: RFC 1238 is an Experimental document that obsoletes RFC 1162. It has not itself been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: The Management Framework
sections.content:
This memo defines an experimental portion of the Management Information Base (MIB) for network management in TCP/IP-based internets. It builds on the Internet-standard Network Management Framework, which has three parts: the SMI (RFC 1155, with a more concise form in RFC 1212), the MIB itself (RFC 1156 and RFC 1213), and SNMP (RFC 1157), the protocol used to reach managed objects.

Each managed object has a name, a syntax and an encoding. The name is an object identifier, the syntax is written in a restricted subset of ASN.1, and the encoding follows the basic encoding rules of ASN.1. The Framework allows new objects to be defined for experimentation and evaluation, which is why this module sits under the experimental subtree.
sections.eli5: There is a standard way to describe things a network helper can ask about. This note adds new questions for one special kind of network.

sections.title: Scope and the ClnpAddress Type
sections.content:
The objects apply when the ISO Connectionless-mode Network Protocol (CLNP, ISO 8473) and the End System to Intermediate System protocol (ES-IS, ISO 9542) are present. No assumption is made about the protocol that carries SNMP. OSI addresses are described textually using a string encoding from a separate research note.

The one new data type is ClnpAddress, an octet string of 1 to 21 octets. The first octet holds a length in the range 0 to 20, and the NSAP follows. A zero-length NSAP means "the default NSAP", like the IP address 0.0.0.0, and is a single octet with value 0. Other NSAPs take at least 4 octets. The RFC stresses that this textual convention changes neither the syntax nor the semantics of any object.
sections.eli5: An address is written as a length followed by the address itself. An address of length zero means "the usual one".

sections.title: Groups of Objects in CLNS-MIB
sections.content:
The module is rooted at clns, placed at { experimental 1 }, and has four groups: clnp, error, echo and es-is.

The CLNP group is recommended for every system that implements CLNP. It begins with clnpForwarding, which says whether the entity acts as an intermediate system (it forwards PDUs not addressed to it) or an end system, and clnpDefaultLifeTime. Most others are counters: PDUs received, header errors, address errors, forwarded, delivered, discarded, reassembly outcomes and segmentation outcomes. Tables cover the entity's CLNP addresses, the routing table, and address translation in both directions between network and physical addresses.

The CLNP Error group is recommended for systems that implement the CLNP Error protocol. It counts error PDUs received and sent, with separate counters for reasons such as checksum errors, congestion, header problems, segmentation, duplicates, unreachable or unknown destinations, source routing problems and unsupported options.

The ES-IS group is recommended for systems that implement ES-IS. It holds six counters: ESH, ISH and RDU PDUs, each received and sent.
sections.eli5: The list is split into drawers. One drawer counts the packets that come and go, one counts the kinds of mistakes, and one counts the hello messages that end systems and routers swap.

sections.title: Changes from RFC 1162
sections.content:
This memo obsoletes RFC 1162. The RFC lists four changes.

  • The objects are redefined using the extended conventions of the SMI, with semantics identical to RFC 1162.
  • The PhysAddress textual convention from MIB-II is introduced to represent media addresses.
  • The objects clnpRoutingDiscards, clnpRouteMetric5 and clnpRouteInfo are defined.
  • The ClnpAddress type was mistakenly given a tag in RFC 1162. This error is corrected.
sections.eli5: This is a tidied second edition. It fixes one mistake and adds a few new things to ask about.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC states only that security issues are not discussed in this memo. Its status text calls it an Experimental Protocol for the Internet community and points readers to the current "IAB Official Protocol Standards" for its standardization state.
sections.eli5: The note does not say anything about keeping this information safe.
